display.purpose: One per page: the index headline, each lesson's title, and the head of the card catalogue, checkride and sources pages. Archivo Narrow only; the normal width wraps the headline and is a different character.

headline.purpose: In-column section heads inside the reading column, and the section heads on the catalogue and sources pages.

title.purpose: The one-line lesson summary under the display title, capped at 40ch; the same role carries the lede on the catalogue, checkride and sources pages.

body.purpose: The reading column at a 68ch measure. Set-apart body steps to 18px (concrete anchor, misconception claim, stage-check question).

label.purpose: All mono chrome: figure references, the step counter, table headers, instrument labels, HUD, plate captions, card captions, launch control. Every numeral in the build lives in this face.

lineWeights.name: hair
lineWeights.purpose: Zone grid, table interiors, quiet boxes, figure detail layer, the airframe's detail linework.

lineWeights.name: rule
lineWeights.purpose: A real border, a leader line, a plot axis; upgraded to ink for an instrument plate.

lineWeights.name: line
lineWeights.purpose: A drawn object's outline in a figure.

lineWeights.name: force
lineWeights.purpose: Figure force arrows only — heavier than any structural line by intent.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The one authored motion: leader lines drawing in, and the figure's step crossfade.

motion.name: dur
motion.purpose: Long transition budget; the leader draw-in runs 620ms with a 46ms per-balloon stagger, the step crossfade 300ms.

components.name: Plate
components.description: The only container this world has: square, hairline, no elevation, with an optional mono caption strip carrying an identifier and a reference.
components.html:
Angle of attack is the angle between the chord line and the relative wind — not the angle to the horizon.
Fig. 3–2Step 4 of 4
components.css: .ds-plate { border: 1px solid var(--rule, #c9c7c0); background: var(--paper, #f4f4f1); color: var(--ink, #14171c); border-radius: 0; font-family: var(--f-body, 'Archivo Variable', system-ui, sans-serif); font-size: 16.5px; line-height: 1.62; } .ds-plate-body { padding: 17px 19px; } .ds-plate-cap { border-top: 0.5px solid var(--rule, #c9c7c0); padding: 7px 12px; display: flex; gap: 14px; align-items: center; font-family: var(--f-mono, 'JetBrains Mono Variable', ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 10px; letter-spacing: .1em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--ink-3, #6b7079); }

components.name: Step Tabs
components.description: The figure's build strip. Three states driven by a data-at attribute of done | now | todo: passed steps take a paper-sunk ground with an ink-3 border, the current step fills solid ink with paper text, steps ahead stay hollow. Never accent — this sits in the lesson's first viewport.
components.html: Fig. 2–2 · Step 3 of 4
components.css: .ds-steps { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 9px 12px; border-top: 0.5px solid var(--rule, #c9c7c0); background: var(--paper, #f4f4f1); } .ds-steps-lab { font-family: var(--f-mono, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 10px; letter-spacing: .12em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--ink-3, #6b7079); margin-right: 4px; } .ds-step { width: 26px; height: 26px; cursor: pointer; background: var(--paper, #f4f4f1); border: 0.5px solid var(--rule, #c9c7c0); border-radius: 0; font-family: var(--f-mono, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 11px; color: var(--ink-2, #454b55); } .ds-step:hover { border-color: var(--ink, #14171c); color: var(--ink, #14171c); } .ds-step:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #d6006e); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-step[data-at="done"] { background: var(--paper-sunk, #eceae5); border-color: var(--ink-3, #6b7079); color: var(--ink-2, #454b55); } .ds-step[data-at="now"], .ds-step[aria-pressed="true"] { background: var(--ink, #14171c); border-color: var(--ink, #14171c); color: var(--paper, #f4f4f1); font-weight: 600; }

components.name: Arrow Mark
components.description: The interface arrow, drawn and never typed: an 18×10 SVG with a 1.1px shaft and a solid triangular head in currentColor, the same flat tail and solid head as the figures' force arrows. Mirrored for the leftward case. A literal arrow glyph anywhere in this build is a defect.
components.html: <svg class="ds-mk" viewBox="0 0 18 10" aria-hidden="true"><path class="ds-mk-s" d="M0 5 H12"/><path class="ds-mk-h" d="M11 1 L18 5 L11 9 Z"/></svg><svg class="ds-mk" viewBox="0 0 18 10" aria-hidden="true"><path class="ds-mk-s" d="M18 5 H6"/><path class="ds-mk-h" d="M7 1 L0 5 L7 9 Z"/></svg>
components.css: .ds-mk { width: 18px; height: 10px; flex: none; display: inline-block; vertical-align: -1px; color: var(--ink, #14171c); } .ds-mk-s { stroke: currentColor; stroke-width: 1.1; fill: none; } .ds-mk-h { fill: currentColor; stroke: none; }

components.name: Assembly Mark
components.description: The wordmark's mark: a plan-view aircraft — nose, wing, fuselage, tailplane — strung down a dash-dot assembly axis, which is the drafting convention that stops four rectangles reading as a bar chart. Drawn from geometry in currentColor, so it inherits ink, survives the negative plate and costs nothing at any size. It is ink like every other drawn thing; it takes the accent only on hover of the title it sits in.
components.html: Flight Dynamics
components.css: .ds-brand { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 9px; color: var(--ink, #14171c); text-decoration: none; font-family: var(--f-body, system-ui, sans-serif); font-size: 12.5px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: .14em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-logo { flex: none; display: block; color: var(--ink, #14171c); } .ds-brand:hover .ds-logo { color: var(--accent, #d6006e); }

components.name: Launch Control
components.description: The primary action of a sandbox lesson, living in the plate's own caption strip as a hairline-topped transparent mono control rather than a filled slab. Label and drawn arrow travel together at the left so they read as one control.
components.css: .ds-launch { display: flex; width: 100%; align-items: center; gap: 9px; padding: 9px 12px; cursor: pointer; text-align: left; background: none; color: var(--ink, #14171c); border: 0; border-top: 0.5px solid var(--rule, #c9c7c0); border-radius: 0; font-family: var(--f-mono, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 10.5px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: .13em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-launch .ds-mk { color: var(--accent, #d6006e); } .ds-launch:hover { background: var(--paper-sunk, #eceae5); } .ds-launch:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #d6006e); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-launch:disabled { color: var(--ink-3, #6b7079); cursor: default; } .ds-launch:disabled .ds-mk { color: var(--ink-3, #6b7079); } .ds-mk { width: 18px; height: 10px; flex: none; } .ds-mk-s { stroke: currentColor; stroke-width: 1.1; fill: none; } .ds-mk-h { fill: currentColor; stroke: none; }

components.name: Misconception Box
components.description: Achromatic set-apart block with a heavy ink top rule over hairline sides — which is what separates it from the check plate — and a drawn revision triangle. No kicker label, no semantic colour.
components.html:
“A wing works because air over the top has further to travel.”

It doesn’t, and the two parcels never meet again. Lift comes from the wing turning the flow downward.
components.css: .ds-myth { border: 0.5px solid var(--rule, #c9c7c0); border-top: 1px solid var(--ink, #14171c); background: var(--paper, #f4f4f1); color: var(--ink, #14171c); border-radius: 0; font-family: var(--f-body, system-ui, sans-serif); line-height: 1.62; } .ds-myth-b { padding: 17px 19px; } .ds-myth-claim { display: flex; gap: 11px; align-items: baseline; font-size: 18px; font-weight: 600; margin: 0 0 .7em; } .ds-revmark { width: 14px; height: 12px; flex: none; fill: var(--ink, #14171c); } .ds-myth-truth { margin: 0; color: var(--ink-2, #454b55); font-size: 16.5px; }

components.name: Stage Check
components.description: A 1px ink plate built as an answer key, not as a stack of buttons. Headed by a plate caption strip reading Stage Check with a chapter reference — an identifier and a reference number, the way a manual heads an inspection block, not a kicker. The question is the heading with no label above it, on a paper-sunk ground closed with a full 1px ink rule. Each option is a contiguous ruled row with a 46px keyed cell carrying a mono A / B / C. Once answered, the answered key cell fills solid with its semantic colour and a drawn tick or cross is stroked on top in paper: stroking the mark in the force colour on paper measured 2.87, under the 3:1 a graphic needs.
components.html:
Stage CheckCh 04 · 3 options

An aircraft in a steady climb: how does thrust compare with drag?

Why: in a climb, thrust also carries part of the weight along the flight path.

} .ds-check-opt:hover:not(:disabled) { background: var(--paper-sunk, #eceae5); } .ds-check-opt:hover:not(:disabled) .ds-check-k { color: var(--ink, #14171c); border-right-color: var(--ink, #14171c); } .ds-check-opt:disabled { cursor: default; text-decoration: line-through; } .ds-check-why { font-size: 15px; color: var(--ink-2, #454b55); margin: 0; padding: 14px 18px; border-top: 1px solid var(--ink, #14171c); }

components.name: Drafting Scale
components.description: A control read like an instrument: mono label, end marks, a ticked track and a square accent thumb, with a right-aligned mono output. The panel is closed with a 1px ink top rule because it is an instrument.
components.html:
Hold the nose up and let the speed decay until the wing lets go.

0%
100%
64%
components.css: .ds-instr { border-top: 1px solid var(--ink, #14171c); background: var(--paper, #f4f4f1); padding: 14px 12px 12px; } .ds-brief { margin: 0 0 14px; font-size: 15px; color: var(--ink-2, #454b55); max-width: 62ch; font-family: var(--f-body, system-ui, sans-serif); } .ds-ctl { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 88px 1fr 62px; gap: 12px; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 12px; } .ds-ctl label { font-family: var(--f-mono, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 10px; letter-spacing: .12em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--ink-2, #454b55); } .ds-ctl output { font-family: var(--f-mono, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 12.5px; text-align: right; color: var(--ink, #14171c); } .ds-scale { display: grid; grid-template-columns: auto 1fr auto; gap: 9px; align-items: center; } .ds-scale span { font-family: var(--f-mono, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 10px; color: var(--ink-3, #6b7079); white-space: nowrap; } .ds-track { position: relative; } .ds-track::after { content: ""; position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; top: 15px; height: 5px; background-image: repeating-linear-gradient(to right, var(--rule, #c9c7c0) 0 1px, transparent 1px 10%); pointer-events: none; } .ds-ctl input[type="range"] { display: block; width: 100%; height: 22px; background: none; -webkit-appearance: none; appearance: none; } .ds-ctl input[type="range"]::-webkit-slider-runnable-track { height: 2px; background: var(--rule, #c9c7c0); } .ds-ctl input[type="range"]::-moz-range-track { height: 2px; background: var(--rule, #c9c7c0); } .ds-ctl input[type="range"]::-webkit-slider-thumb { -webkit-appearance: none; width: 12px; height: 20px; margin-top: -9px; background: var(--accent, #d6006e); border: 0; border-radius: 0; cursor: grab; } .ds-ctl input[type="range"]::-moz-range-thumb { width: 12px; height: 20px; background: var(--accent, #d6006e); border: 0; border-radius: 0; cursor: grab; }

components.name: Force Readout
components.description: Four hairline cells, each a mono caption over a value coloured by its own force (two cells below 620px). The only chrome that carries semantic colour, because each cell IS a force. The same grid carries the card catalogue's session counts, where due takes drag and mastered takes thrust.
components.css: .ds-readout { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr); border: 0.5px solid var(--rule, #c9c7c0); background: var(--paper, #f4f4f1); } .ds-readout > div { padding: 8px 10px; border-right: 0.5px solid var(--rule, #c9c7c0); min-width: 0; } .ds-readout > div:last-child { border-right: 0; } .ds-readout span { display: block; font-family: var(--f-mono, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 10px; letter-spacing: .1em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--ink-3, #6b7079); } .ds-readout b { display: block; font-family: var(--f-mono, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 15px; font-weight: 500; margin-top: 2px; } .ds-v-lift b { color: var(--f-lift, #1971c2); } .ds-v-weight b { color: var(--f-weight, #14171c); } .ds-v-thrust b { color: var(--f-thrust, #2f9e44); } .ds-v-drag b { color: var(--f-drag, #e03131); } @media (max-width: 620px) { .ds-readout { grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr); } .ds-readout > div:nth-child(2) { border-right: 0; } .ds-readout > div:nth-child(-n+2) { border-bottom: 0.5px solid var(--rule, #c9c7c0); } }

components.name: Balloon Callout
components.description: The numbered ring on a leader line: the index plate's only navigation. Fills solid ink once its lesson is complete. Keyboard-operable, with the parts table as the accessible path.

components.css: .ds-stage { display: block; background: var(--paper, #f4f4f1); } .ds-balloon { cursor: pointer; } .ds-lead { stroke: var(--ink-3, #6b7079); stroke-width: 1px; fill: none; } .ds-ring { fill: var(--paper, #f4f4f1); stroke: var(--ink, #14171c); stroke-width: 1px; } .ds-num { fill: var(--ink, #14171c); font-family: var(--f-mono, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; text-anchor: middle; dominant-baseline: central; } .ds-name { fill: var(--ink-2, #454b55); font-family: var(--f-mono, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 10px; letter-spacing: .1em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-balloon:hover .ds-lead, .ds-balloon:focus-visible .ds-lead { stroke: var(--accent, #d6006e); stroke-width: 1.5px; } .ds-balloon:hover .ds-ring, .ds-balloon:focus-visible .ds-ring { stroke: var(--accent, #d6006e); } .ds-balloon:hover .ds-num, .ds-balloon:focus-visible .ds-num { fill: var(--accent, #d6006e); } .ds-balloon:hover .ds-name, .ds-balloon:focus-visible .ds-name { fill: var(--ink, #14171c); } .ds-done .ds-ring { fill: var(--ink, #14171c); } .ds-done .ds-num { fill: var(--paper, #f4f4f1); }

components.name: Parts Index Row
components.description: The parts table carrying real lessons: mono item number, body-weight link, secondary remarks, and a mono status that reads complete in thrust green. The same table is reused for the checkride's item list and the sources page's channel list. Below 620px each row becomes its own two-column grid and the header is dropped.
components.html:
ItemLessonRemarks
01The four forcesEverything an aircraft does is these four, in balance or not.complete
02LiftThe wing turns the flow down; the flow pushes the wing up.
components.css: .ds-index { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; background: var(--paper, #f4f4f1); color: var(--ink, #14171c); font-family: var(--f-body, system-ui, sans-serif); font-size: 16.5px; line-height: 1.62; } .ds-index th { text-align: left; font-family: var(--f-mono, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 10px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: .12em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--ink-3, #6b7079); padding: 8px 12px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--ink, #14171c); } .ds-index td { padding: 11px 12px; border-bottom: 0.5px solid var(--rule-soft, #dedcd5); vertical-align: baseline; } .ds-index tr:hover td { background: var(--paper-sunk, #eceae5); } .ds-index a { color: inherit; text-decoration: none; font-weight: 600; } .ds-index a:hover { color: var(--accent, #d6006e); } .ds-c-item { width: 62px; font-family: var(--f-mono, ui-monospace, monospace); color: var(--ink-3, #6b7079); font-size: 12.5px; } .ds-c-rem { color: var(--ink-2, #454b55); font-size: 14px; } .ds-c-st { width: 92px; text-align: right; font-family: var(--f-mono, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 10px; letter-spacing: .1em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--ink-3, #6b7079); } .ds-done-row .ds-c-st { color: var(--f-thrust, #2f9e44); } @media (max-width: 620px) { .ds-index { display: block; border-top: 1px solid var(--ink, #14171c); } .ds-index thead { display: none; } .ds-index tbody { display: block; } .ds-index tr { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 38px minmax(0, 1fr); column-gap: 10px; padding: 11px 12px; border-bottom: 0.5px solid var(--rule-soft, #dedcd5); } .ds-index td { display: block; padding: 0; border: 0; } .ds-c-item { width: auto; grid-column: 1; grid-row: 1; } .ds-index tr td:nth-child(2) { grid-column: 2; grid-row: 1; } .ds-c-rem { grid-column: 2; grid-row: 2; margin-top: 4px; } .ds-c-st { grid-column: 2; grid-row: 3; width: auto; text-align: left; margin-top: 6px; } .ds-c-st:empty { display: none; } }

components.name: Catalogue Entry
components.description: The way into the card catalogue, the checkride and the sources page: a 1px ink bar sitting under the parts table as a manual's back matter, mono title with a mono count and a drawn arrow pushed to the right. Stacked entries share one rule (margin-top: -1px). Reachable only from the foot of the index — spaced repetition you have to go hunting for does not get used, and burying it inside a chapter is worse.
components.html: Card catalogue36 cards · 8 due
components.css: .ds-catalogue { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 14px; padding: 14px 16px; text-decoration: none; color: var(--ink, #14171c); border: 1px solid var(--ink, #14171c); border-radius: 0; background: var(--paper, #f4f4f1); } .ds-catalogue-t { font-family: var(--f-mono, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: .13em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-catalogue-n { font-family: var(--f-mono, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 10.5px; letter-spacing: .08em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--ink-3, #6b7079); } .ds-catalogue .ds-mk { margin-left: auto; color: var(--accent, #d6006e); } .ds-catalogue:hover { background: var(--paper-sunk, #eceae5); } .ds-mk { width: 18px; height: 10px; flex: none; } .ds-mk-s { stroke: currentColor; stroke-width: 1.1; fill: none; } .ds-mk-h { fill: currentColor; stroke: none; }

components.name: Card
components.description: A card is a plate: 1px ink border, a hairline-bottomed mono caption strip carrying the chapter and the card's kind, the prompt at 19px, and the answer on a paper-sunk well. Its content is DERIVED from the lessons' misconceptions, formulas and stage-check questions; there is no card text in the codebase. Study grades itself into Leitner boxes with two hairline grade buttons (the recalled one resolving to thrust, the missed one to drag); examination reuses the stage check's keyed rows and scores without self-grading.
components.html:
Ch 02misconception

What is wrong with this?

A wing works because air over the top has further to travel.
It doesn’t, and the two parcels never meet again. Lift comes from the wing turning the flow downward.
components.css: .ds-card { border: 1px solid var(--ink, #14171c); background: var(--paper, #f4f4f1); color: var(--ink, #14171c); border-radius: 0; margin-bottom: 16px; font-family: var(--f-body, system-ui, sans-serif); line-height: 1.62; } .ds-card-cap { display: flex; gap: 14px; padding: 7px 12px; border-bottom: 0.5px solid var(--rule, #c9c7c0); font-family: var(--f-mono, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 10px; letter-spacing: .12em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--ink-3, #6b7079); } .ds-card-cap span:last-child { margin-left: auto; } .ds-card-lead { margin: 0; padding: 13px 18px 0; font-family: var(--f-mono, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 10px; letter-spacing: .1em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--ink-3, #6b7079); } .ds-card-q { padding: 16px 18px; font-size: 19px; line-height: 1.45; } .ds-card-a { padding: 15px 18px; border-top: 0.5px solid var(--rule, #c9c7c0); background: var(--paper-sunk, #eceae5); color: var(--ink-2, #454b55); font-size: 15.5px; } .ds-card-grade { display: flex; gap: 12px; } .ds-card-grade button { flex: 1; cursor: pointer; background: none; border-radius: 0; border: 0.5px solid var(--rule, #c9c7c0); padding: 14px 16px; color: var(--ink-2, #454b55); font-family: var(--f-mono, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 11px; letter-spacing: .1em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-card-grade button:hover { border-color: var(--f-drag, #e03131); color: var(--ink, #14171c); } .ds-card-grade .right:hover { border-color: var(--f-thrust, #2f9e44); } @media (max-width: 620px) { .ds-card-grade { flex-direction: column; } }

components.name: Checkride Item Bar
components.description: The final test, flown rather than answered: a hairline-closed mono bar naming the item, with a row of 9px square progress marks (passed fills thrust, current fills ink, ahead is a hollow rule square) and the item's name at 19px beneath. The advance control is a mono button bordered in thrust — a completion fact, the same licence the index takes for complete. Each item resets the aircraft to its own start.
components.html:

components.name: Video Plate
components.description: Clips play here, never off-site. A native <dialog> that is a full paper takeover, not a dimmed lightbox — this world has no translucency layer, and turning to a clip is turning to another plate, so ::backdrop is solid paper. A 1px ink border, a mono bar carrying channel, duration and a drawn close cross, a 16:9 stage on paper-sunk, and a caption below. When the clip ends the end card offers the lesson and the next clip in-world, which is the moment YouTube would have offered three more.

narrative.overview:
The artifact is an aircraft maintenance manual that happens to be interactive. Every page is a numbered plate on index stock: a ruled zone-grid margin runs down all four sides carrying letter and number ticks, a rule-bottomed title bar names the plate and its chapter, and the content sits inside hairline boxes with square corners and no shadow anywhere. Chrome is drawn, not styled — borders, rules and line weights do all the structural work that a conventional interface would give to fills, radii and elevation.

The system's single organising decision is that colour is a scarce, meaningful substance. The interface itself spends none of it: everything the reader clicks, reads or navigates by is paper, ink and grey. That budget is handed entirely to the physics — lift is blue, thrust is green, drag is red, weight is ink — so that a coloured mark anywhere on the page can only ever be a statement about forces. One accent exists, a chart magenta borrowed from the airspace rings on a sectional, and it is deliberately absent from the semantic set so the interface can never be mistaken for data. It appears in slivers: a focus ring, a caret, a slider thumb, a hover state, a formula's term key, one drawn arrow.

Dark mode is not an inversion filter but a negative plate — the same drawing seen on a light table, white line on black. It is written out as a duplicated token block rather than routed through a second indirection layer, because two readable blocks beat one clever one. The raster plate on the index flips with it (multiply on the positive plate, inverted and screened on the negative), so the illustration is the same document either way.

The positive plate is the default, not the system setting. This is a drawing on index stock; the negative is the alternate reading of it, and a reader whose OS happens to be dark should still meet the document as drawn. The control reads light / dark / auto in those words — positive and negative are the right names for the system and the wrong ones for a button, since nobody can tell which way round they go without pressing it.

The course ends where a real one does. Beyond the twelve chapters the index carries a card catalogue whose cards are derived from the lessons rather than authored beside them, a checkride that is flown rather than answered, and a sources page. All three are plates with the same furniture as every other plate.
keyCharacteristics: Square corners everywhere (0 radius); the only exception is the label chip inside figures (4px)
Exactly three line weights: hairline (0.5px), rule (1px), line (1.5px)
Zero elevation — no box-shadow exists anywhere in the build, and the video plate is a paper takeover rather than a dimmed lightbox
Achromatic chrome and a semantic force palette that never mix
One rationed accent, absent from the semantic set
All numerals, labels and instrument readings in mono, tabular
Every mark is drawn from geometry — the arrows, the tick and cross, the revision triangle, the CG symbol, the wordmark's assembly axis. No glyph icons, no icon set
One authored motion moment (leader lines drawing in); everything else is a state change

rules.name: The Two Palettes Rule
rules.body: Chrome is achromatic; semantic colour carries meaning and nothing else. A colour on this page is a claim about physics, so chrome never wears one. A drag-red border on a callout reads as a drag annotation — the misconception box is therefore achromatic with a drawn revision triangle, and the current step tab is ink, not accent. The two standing exceptions are results, not decoration: the index's `complete` in thrust green, and the answered key cell in the stage check.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one accent, and it is absent from the semantic set. It is rationed to marks measured in pixels: a focus ring, a caret, a thumb, a hover, one drawn arrow. A filled accent slab anywhere in a first viewport spends the whole colour budget on chrome and is a defect, not a variant.

rules.name: The Negative Plate Rule
rules.body: Dark mode is the same drawing on a light table, not a generic inversion. The positive plate is the default rather than the system setting, and the control reads light / dark / auto. Both the prefers-color-scheme path and the explicit data-plate="negative" attribute carry the full duplicated token block, and any treatment that depends on plate polarity (the raster's blend mode) must handle both paths or the auto-dark reader gets black on black.

rules.name: The One Ramp Rule
rules.body: Five roles, and that is the whole system: display, headline, title, body, label. A new surface picks a role; it does not invent a size. Figure-internal type is not on this ramp — it is set in SVG user units inside the viewBox so it scales with the plate rather than with the page.

rules.name: The Mono Numeral Rule
rules.body: Every numeral the reader might compare — instrument readouts, force values, table item numbers, step counters, figure numbers, balloon numbers, card counts, checkride scores — is JetBrains Mono with tabular figures, so digits stay in column as they change. Prose numerals inherit font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums from body for the same reason.

rules.name: The Frame Margin Rule
rules.body: The frame's padding is rail + gap, never rail alone. --rail-gap (18px, 8px on a phone) is the air between the index rail and the drawing it indexes; set to the rail width exactly, the type butts against the rail's hairline and the margin has no margin in it. The foot is rail + 52px, because the bottom rail is fixed and opaque — a frame that does not reserve its height leaves the last 34px of every document permanently underneath it, which is what made the twelfth lesson unreachable on the index.

rules.name: The Flat Plate Rule
rules.body: Nothing floats. A surface is distinguished from its neighbour by border weight or by one tonal step, never by a shadow, and never by lifting on hover. Even the video dialog is a full paper takeover with a solid paper ::backdrop, because this world has no translucency layer.

rules.name: The One Animation Rule
rules.body: The plate draws itself in once, on load. Every other movement in the build is a state change or the figure's 300ms step crossfade, not an animation.

rules.name: The Drawn Mark Rule
rules.body: Every mark in this world is drawn from geometry, at the weights the figures use. The interface arrow is an 18×10 SVG with a 1.1px shaft and a solid head (.mk, mirrored for the leftward case); the stage check's result is a stroked tick or cross; the misconception carries a revision triangle; the wordmark is four rectangles on a dash-dot assembly axis. A typed → or ← glyph, or an imported icon set, is a different object at a different weight and is a defect.

rules.name: The Assembly Step Rule
rules.body: A figure is one drawing at successive stages of its own assembly — "Step", never "sheet", because in a real parts catalogue Sheet 2 of 4 is a different page carrying different content and readers concluded they were missing three other figures. It assembles on the APPROACH to its reference and is complete when the reference reaches the reading line; each approach is capped to the room actually available between two references, or a tight chapter has the next figure stealing the bench before the current one's prose has been read. The strip names the plate and then the step — Fig. 2–2 · Step 3 of 3 — because seven of the twelve lessons give every figure the same step count and a strip reading only Step 3 of 3 looked frozen.

rules.name: The Receding Airframe Rule
rules.body: The forces are the subject; the aeroplane is what they act on, and it is drawn as the quieter mark. Every airframe — the airframe group in figures, the built geometry in the sandbox — sits at ink-2 for its outline and ink-3 for its detail layer, so the four force arrows are the brightest marks on the plate. The CG mark stays at full ink: it is a datum, not part of the body. This is correctness, not preference: on the negative plate --f-weight resolves to --ink, so a full-ink airframe and the weight arrow are the same colour exactly (contrast 1.00) and the one force the reader is looking for disappears into the fuselage.

rules.name: The Legible Scene Rule
rules.body: The sandbox is the same world in three dimensions, reading every colour from the same custom properties. Three things in it are load-bearing: a body fills to paper-sunk and never to the scene background (filled with --paper it measured 1.00 and read as a hole punched in the picture); the ground is ink at 0.16 and is exempt from fog (at 0.05 under fog, ground-to-sky was 1.11 — no ground and no horizon, only haze), while fog still applies to the runway stripes where fading with distance is the point; and the horizon is drawn in ink-3, not rule, which lands within 1.06 of the ground and vanishes.

rules.name: The Derived Deck Rule
rules.body: Cards are derived in src/data/deck.js from the misconceptions, formulas and stage-check questions the lessons already carry; there is no card text in the codebase. A hand-written deck drifts, and a drifted card teaches the old thing long after the lesson was corrected. Study grades itself into Leitner boxes (1/2/4/8/16 sessions); examination scores the same material with no self-grading.

rules.name: The Honest Model Rule
rules.body: A chapter gets a sandbox only if the model can demonstrate its idea honestly, and the checkride only asks the learner to produce claims the model can judge. MISSING stays in tasks.js even while empty, because miming a manoeuvre the model is not computing would be worse than having no sandbox at all. Every checkride item resets the aircraft to its own start, and scripts/check-checkride.mjs flies all of them on each npm run check — an unreachable item fails the build.

dos: Do keep chrome achromatic. Paper, ink, grey and one rationed accent is the whole interface palette.
Do reserve the semantic palette for statements about physics, and address it by kind, never by colour value.
Do draw structure with the three line weights — hairline 0.5px, rule 1px, line 1.5px — and upgrade to a 1px ink border when a container is an instrument.
Do use a thin ruled box for set-apart text (the concrete anchor and misconception boxes are both hairline boxes).
Do let a progressive figure assemble on the approach to its reference, and cap each approach to the room between two references.
Do give the step strip three states — passed on paper-sunk with an ink-3 border, current solid ink, ahead hollow — so it reads as a build.
Do draw every mark from geometry at the figures' weights: the arrows, the tick and cross, the revision triangle, the wordmark.
Do pad the frame by rail + gap on the sides and rail + 52px at the foot, because the bottom rail is fixed and opaque.
Do set every numeral, label and instrument reading in JetBrains Mono with tabular figures.
Do size a force arrow by its magnitude. In the sandbox, arrow length IS the measurement; only the label may be clamped to stay in frame.
Do draw airframes at ink-2 outline and ink-3 detail so the force arrows are the brightest marks on the plate.
Do carry both dark-mode paths (prefers-color-scheme and data-plate="negative") when a treatment depends on plate polarity, and keep the positive plate the default.
Do hold body text to the 68ch measure and keep the index plate at 900px minimum on small screens, scrolling sideways rather than shrinking.
Do derive card content from the lessons, so a corrected chapter corrects its cards.
donts: Don't put a semantic colour on chrome. A drag-red callout border reads as a drag annotation; a misconception box is achromatic.
Don't fill the current step tab — or any first-viewport block — with the accent. That control is solid ink.
Don't call a figure's stages sheets, or open one on the finished drawing. They are steps in one assembly, built on the approach to the reference.

Don't add a kicker or eyebrow label above a block. "Common misconception", "Check yourself" and their kind do not exist here; the drawn revision triangle and the question itself carry the flag. A plate caption strip carrying an identifier and a reference number (Stage Check · Ch 04 · 3 options) is the manual's own inspection heading and is the only licence.
Don't type an arrow glyph or import an icon set. Every mark in this world is drawn from geometry at the figures' weights.
Don't build a coloured left-bar callout. Set-apart text gets a hairline ruled box; an aside gets a hairline left rule in rule grey.
Don't introduce a corner radius. Every chrome element is square.
Don't add a shadow, a blur, a translucency layer or a lift-on-hover. There is no elevation in this system, and the video plate is a paper takeover rather than a dimmed lightbox.
Don't add a second accent, or reuse the accent inside the semantic set — its absence there is what keeps interface from reading as data.
Don't add a fourth line weight or a sixth type role.
Don't draw an airframe at full ink, in a figure or in the sandbox. It out-shouts the forces, and on the negative plate it is the same value as the weight arrow.
Don't fill a 3D body with the scene background colour, and don't let fog eat the ground. Both were shipped once and both erased the horizon. The horizon itself is ink-3, not rule.
Don't link a video off-site. Clips play in the in-app plate; the end of one offers the lesson and the next clip, never YouTube's grid.
Don't leave a reader inside a chapter with no way out. The wordmark links home but reads as a title, so the bar carries an explicit Index control and the footer's middle slot carries All 12 chapters.
Don't give a chapter a sandbox the model cannot honestly compute. Add the physics, or leave the chapter without one and record why in tasks.js.
Don't author flashcard text. Cards derive from the lessons; anything hand-written beside them drifts out of step and then teaches the old answer.
Don't turn the checkride into a skills course. Every item must be a claim from a chapter, judged by the model, and passable by understanding rather than by dexterity.
Don't animate anything new. The plate's leader lines draw in once; everything else is a state change.
Don't put figure labels in a legend, or pass a colour into a figure primitive.
